## Summary

A two-hour cross-asset mean-reversion rule: **when the S&P 500 opens with a big gap, take the other side in BTC.** S&P gaps up → short BTC at 9:35 New York; gaps down → buy it; close at 11:35. A "big gap" = **≥1.5× the S&P's typical opening move over the trailing 60 sessions** (1× on the first session of a week).

Claimed results, Hyperliquid, March 2025–Nov 2026 (58 trades = 30 gap-up + 28 gap-down):

- **Sharpe 2.06 after fees**, +0.45%/trade, 60% winners, worst drawdown 4.0%.
- **The mirror loses:** trading WITH the gap instead costs −0.65%/trade.
- **Out-of-sample discipline:** rule received as-is from @skepticalxbt, "we didn't tune it", and it also held on **195 trades back to 2022**.
- **Multiple-testing check:** 500 randomized versions (random days, random side) all did worse.
- **Fragility disclosed:** entering an hour late kills the edge — the open is what matters.
- Chart (average path from 9:35): gap-up days drift −0.4%→−0.6% into 11:05–11:35; gap-down days +0.58%; other sessions +0.03% (n = 30/28/348). Source: Hyperliquid BTC 5-min candles + Yahoo S&P open/close.

## Why it matters

- **This is the [[2026-10-01-algojan-nq-monday-short]] genre — time-gated index fade — executed with the rigor that genre almost never shows:** the rule came from outside (hypothesis-first testing, per [[2026-10-01-dmartin-hypothesis-first]]), no tuning is claimed, it held out-of-sample back to 2022 (195 trades), and the 500-random-versions check is a poor-man's PBO in the spirit of [[2026-10-28-margincall4-overfitting-validation-dsr-pbo-walkforward]]. Even the entry-time sensitivity is disclosed rather than hidden.
- **Economic mechanism is plausible:** a large S&P gap is a liquidity/panic event; BTC's 24/7 book absorbs the displaced flow and mean-reverts once equities stabilize. The chart's clean separation (+0.58% fade-day vs −0.5% gap-up path) is what a real risk-premium looks like — but it's also what a 19-month BTC–S&P coupling regime looks like.
- **Skepticism gates:** self-reported, and everything hangs on fee/slippage assumptions at Hyperliquid for 2-hour holds (+0.45%/trade is thin — taker fees both ways on a perp would eat most of it, so the backtest presumably assumes maker or net-of-feats fills); 58 live-window trades with worst-DD 4% is small-sample comfort; and the S&P→BTC linkage is regime-dependent — a 2022–2026 sample spans exactly one coupling era. The OOS 195-trade count is the single most load-bearing claim and is unverifiable from the tweet.
- Actionable: replication task filed (below) — pull Hyperliquid 5-min candles + S&P opens, rebuild the 30/28 gap-day sample, check the fee assumption before this earns any sizing. Same-day intraday companion: [[2026-11-02-margincall4-bos-intraday-l-s-qqq-variants]].
